questions.question: Which branch of economics deals with the depletion of natural resources stock and pollution, which are a result of rapid economic development?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Environmental Economics**__.

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

__
 
• **Environmental Economics deals with the depletion of natural resources stock and pollution, which are a result of rapid economic development**__.

 __
 
• It conducts **theoretical or empirical studies** of the economic impacts of **national or local environmental policies** around the world.
 
• Some specific issues include the costs and benefits of alternative environmental policies to combat air pollution, water quality, solid waste, and global warming.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Developmental Economics -**

 
 
• it is a **branch of economics** that focuses on improving fiscal, economic, and social conditions in developing countries.
 
• it is mainly focused such as **health, education, working conditions, domestic and international policies**, and market conditions.
 
 
 
• **International Economics -**
 
 
• It is concerned with all those economic deals which are done **outside the borders of the country.**​
 
 
 
• **Public Economics -**
 
 
• It is based on the** principle of welfare economics **and is ultimately used as a tool to** improve social welfare.**​
 
 
 
• **​Adam Smith** is known as** 'Father of economics'.**

questions.question: What is the chemical symbol of magnesium?

__
 
• Magnesium (Mg)-

 
 
• It is a chemical element, its atomic number is 12.
 
• In the periodic table, it is denoted by 'Mg'. It is an alkaline element.
 
• It is one of the five major chemical elements found in the human body.
 
• 50% of the magnesium present in the human body is found in bones.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Magnesium -

 
 
• It is very strong even though it is a light element.
 
• For this reason, it is considered useful for alloys and the space industry.
 
• It is found in green leafy vegetables.
 
• It is very important for keeping the immune system, nerves and heart, and bones strong.
 
• It is needed for the heart and kidneys to function properly.
 
• It was discovered by Humphry Davy in 1808.

questions.question: Which of the following is **NOT **a disease caused by a virus?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is ​__**Plague**__.

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

__
 
• **Plague -**

 
 
• **It is an infection caused by a bacteria called "Yersinia pestis"__.**
 
• This bacteria is mainly found in rats or in fleas that bite rats.
 
• There are two main forms of plague - bubonic and pneumonic (when the plague spreads rapidly to the lungs).​
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

 
• **Zika -**

 
 
• It is a **mosquito-borne disease** caused by a **virus.**
 
• The virus is mainly transmitted to humans through the bite of an **infected Aedes mosquito.**
 
 
 
• **AIDS -**
 
 
• The **full name of AIDS **is **Acquired Immune Deficiency Syndrome.**
 
• It is a contagious venereal disease. It is caused by the HIV virus.
 
• The full name of HIV is Human Immune Deficiency Virus (HIV).
 
 
 
• **Ebola -**
 
 
• This is an **infectious disease.**
 
• The disease is** spread through sweat and saliva.**
 
• It is also spread through direct contact with infected blood and feces.​

questions.question: _______ is a process in which impure water is boiled and the steam is collected and condensed in a separate container, leaving many of the solid contaminants behind.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Distillation**__.

__
 
• **Distillation is a process in which impure water is boiled and the steam is collected and condensed in a separate container, leaving many of the solid contaminants behind**__.

 __
 
• By this method, **different components of crude oil **are separated.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Decantation -**

 
 
• It is the **process of separation** of liquid from solid (non-mixing).
 
• Water can be separated by the method of disposal of a mixture of sand and water.
 
• The components of a liquid and its insoluble matter can be separated by the use of filtration.​
 
 
 
• **Sedimentation -**
 
 
• The settling of** particles present in a liquid** on the ground is called sedimentation.
 
• It is** caused by the force of gravity or centrifugal force **acting on the particles suspended in the liquid.
 
 
 
• **Filtration -**
 
 
• In this process, the **solid particles are separated from a liquid or gaseous **substance with the help of filter paper, it is called filtration.​

questions.question: Which longitude has been selected as the Standard Meridian of India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**82°30'E**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Standard Meridian of India (82°30'E) passes through Mirzapur (in Uttar Pradesh)**__.

 __
 
• It is **5 hours 30 minutes ahead **of **Greenwich Mean Time.**
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• ​Indian Standard Time Line **passes through 5 states -**

 
 
• Uttar Pradesh, Madhya Pradesh, Chhattisgarh, Orissa, Andhra Pradesh.
 
 
 
• **Standard line -**
 
 
• The meridian drawn on the earth at **0° longitude** is called the prime meridian or **Greenwich line.**
 
• The standard time of the world is determined by this line.
 
• **Greenwich,** a city in London, is** located on this line**, hence it is also called **'Greenwich Line'.**

questions.question: ______ is made of lower density felsic rocks, such as andesite and granite.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Continental crust**__.

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

__
 
• **Continental crust is made of light rocks like granite**__.** **

 __
 
• It is thick and high above sea level. like **Eurasian and Antarctic Plate**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• ** Oceanic plate:**

 
 
• They have more **weight and less thickness.**
 
• It is formed by** basalt consisting **of the ocean floor. such as the **Pacific Ocean Plate.**
 
 
 
• **​The inner part of the earth** is divided into** three parts -​**
 
 
• **​The Crust**
 
 
• This is the outside layer of the earth and is made of solid rock, mostly basalt and granite.
 
• There are two types of a crust; oceanic and continental. Oceanic crust is denser and thinner and mainly composed of basalt. It is also known as Sima (most abundant minerals being silicate and magnesium)
 
• Continental crust is less dense, thicker, and mainly composed of granite. It is also called Sial (the most abundant minerals being silicate and aluminum).
 
 
 
• **The Mantle**
 
 
• The portion of the interior beyond the crust is called the mantle. The mantle extends from Moho’s discontinuity (the boundary between the crust and mantle) to a depth of 2,900 km.
 
• The crust and the uppermost part of the mantle are called the lithosphere. Its thickness ranges from 10-200 km.
 
• The upper portion of the mantle is called the asthenosphere which is the main source of magma that finds its way to the surface during volcanic eruptions.
 
• The lower mantle extends beyond the asthenosphere. It is in solid-state.
 
 
 
• **The Core**
 
 
• The mantle-core boundary (Gutenberg discontinuity) is located at a depth of 2,900 km.
 
• The outer core is in a liquid state while the inner core is in a solid-state.
 
• The core is made up of very heavy material mostly constituted by nickel and iron. Thus, it is sometimes referred to as the nife layer.
 
 
 
 

71:T

questions.question: Which of the following statements is correct?

options.text: If the constituents of the medium oscillate along the direction of wave propagation, we call the wave a transverse wave
Frequency of a wave is the number of oscillations of each constituent particle in the vibrating medium per minute
If the constituents of the medium oscillate perpendicular to the direction of wave propagation, we call the wave a longitudinal wave.
The minimum distance between two points in a wave having the same phase at a particular instant of time is called the wave length.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**option 4.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Wavelength -**

 
 
• It is a measure of the distance between two equal peaks of a crest or trough.
 
• It is denoted by the Greek letter 'lambda' (λ). Its SI unit is a **'Meter'.**
 
• There is a relationship between the wavelength (λ), the velocity (v) of the wave, and the frequency (f) of a wave.
 
• **λ = v / f**
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Transverse Waves -

 
 
• The mechanical wave which, when transmitted, vibrates perpendicular to the direction of propagation of the particle of the medium, is called a transverse wave.
 
• Transverse waves can only be produced in solids.
 
• These waves cannot be produced inside liquids.
 
• It can be produced only on the surface of the liquid.
 
 
 
• Longitudinal Wave -
 
 
• If the particles of the medium oscillate back and forth at their mean position in the direction of propagation of the wave, then such waves produced are called longitudinal waves. Like sound waves.
 
• Longitudinal waves can be produced in all mediums (solids, liquids, gases).
 
• Sound waves in the air, earthquake waves, and spring waves are also longitudinal waves.​
 
 
 
• **Electromagnetic or mechanical wave -**
 
 
• Waves that do not require any medium for propagation.
 
• That is, these waves can also propagate in a vacuum.
 
 
 
• ** Mechanical Waves -**
 
 
• The disturbance produced by throwing bricks in the water of a calm river or pond is called a mechanical wave.
 
• For mechanical waves to propagate through a medium, it is necessary that the medium has the properties of elasticity or inertia.

questions.question: Who has the power to recommend the dismissal of the state government and suspension or dissolution of the state assembly?
questions.solution:

• **The governor can dissolve the cabinet in the following circumstances**__.

 __
 
• If the governor is convinced that the **majority of the cabinet in the assembly has ended.**

• In such a situation, if the Chief Minister is not ready to call the meeting, then the **Governor can remove the cabinet.**

• The Prime Minister is** the head of the Council of Ministers** of the Central Government and the Chief Advisor to the President.
 
 
 
• **Chief Minister -**
 
 
• He is the **political head of the states **in India.
 
• **Governor administers the oath** of office to the **Chief Minister.**
 
 
 
• **Speaker of the Assembly -**
 
 
• It is** the head of the Legislative Assembly and the Assembly Secretariat**, the Presiding Officer (President).
 
• His **authority is supreme in the premises** of the Legislative Assembly.
 
• It is their responsibility to** maintain the order of the assembly.**
 
• The Speaker **ensures the observance of the rules **from the members of the assembly.
 
• **The Speaker does not participate in the debates** of the Assembly, rather he gives his arrangements/decisions during the proceedings of the Legislative Assembly.
 
• The Speaker presides over the assembly and in his absence, the Deputy Speaker presides over the assembly.​
